A mathematical comparison of three chosen structures

The research compares three mathematical structures. One broad measurement makes them look alike. A more detailed count gives three different answers: 744, 24 and 0.

Switch the view to see the counts. They separate these three chosen structures. They do not prove that a physical object contains the structure nicknamed the Monster.

Compare the broad view with the detailed count. Which view tells the three structures apart?

Words used here
model
A simplified description used to explore a question. A result in the model needs further evidence before it describes the real world.
Read the fuller explanation

Three rank-24 candidates share the same coarse thermal signature. Their weight-one current dimensions—744, 24 and 0—separate the declared E₈³, Leech and Moonshine family.

Even that is one gate on a longer path. The physical carrier, boundary algebra and exclusive detector prediction still have to be established.

The rank-24 detector ladder

E₈³, Leech and Moonshine candidates share a coarse thermal signature. Their weight-one current dimensions are 744, 24 and 0. The three-way distinction is not an unrestricted uniqueness theorem or evidence that a physical system realizes the Monster.
